name: Scuttle Coast
summary: Between Razor Hill and Tiragarde Keep, wreckage from Daelin Proudmoore’s fleet litters Durotar’s eastern shore. The sunken ships make the Scuttle Coast a place where the Horde scavenges and remembers the recent naval war.

sections.title: Wreckage of the Fleet
sections.body: Sunken warships line Durotar’s eastern edge, where the shore meets the Great Sea. During Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s invasion, the Kul Tiras fleet attacked the young nation of Durotar. Fierce battles with the Horde drove many human warships onto jagged shoals, where they broke apart. Barnacled timber, broken rigging, cargo barrels, and sunken ships still mark the coast. For the nearby encampments at Razor Hill, the wreckage recalls how close the Kul Tiran threat remains.

sections.title: Scavengers and Tides
sections.body: The name Scuttle Coast may refer to warships scuttled or grounded in the fighting, or to crabs and makrura picking through the wreckage. Shoreline beasts and dangerous tides keep casual travelers away.

faq.q: Where did all these shipwrecks come from?
faq.answer: The shattered ships belonged to Kul Tiras’s fleet under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. During his failed campaign against the newly founded Horde, they smashed against Durotar’s rocky shallows.

faq.q: Why is it called the Scuttle Coast?
aliases: why is it called scuttle coast
faq.answer: No one is certain. The name may refer to warships scuttled along the coast during naval combat, or to makrura and crabs scuttling across the rocky sands.

faq.q: Is the Scuttle Coast safe to travel?
faq.answer: No. Treacherous waves and jagged rocks line the shore, while makrura and other hostile coastal beasts prowl the surf. Armed Kul Tiras survivors remain entrenched just to the south at Tiragarde Keep.

angles.text: For the Horde, the broken hulls on this beach recall Durotar’s defense against Daelin Proudmoore’s invading navy.
